title: Board speed by sponsor
question: Do files carried by particular sponsors reach a vote faster or slower than like files?
finding: 979 of the 2,326 timed files name no sponsor and 466 name the Mayor. Among the 19 supervisors with ten or more sponsored files, the average gap against like files runs from -9 days (Matt Haney, 47 files) to +23 days (Stephen Sherrill, 12 files); 13 of the 19 are within a week of their peers. 1 of the 19 lies outside the range that random sets of the same number of files fall in 95% of the time (Matt Haney, faster, -9 days), where chance alone would give about 1.
how: Sponsors are those listed on each file in the Board’s records; a file with several sponsors counts once for each, and "as first-named" counts the files where the sponsor is listed first. Days and like files are as in the department screen. Sponsors with fewer than ten timed files are left out. The chance column marks a sponsor whose average lies outside the range that 1,000 random sets of the same number of timed files fall in 95% of the time. Ranked fastest first.
limits: Sponsoring a file is an ordinary part of a supervisor’s work. Sponsors’ sets of files differ in kind as well as number, and like-file matching removes only part of that. Differences of a week or two can follow from when in the year a member’s files were introduced. Nothing here measures how a member voted, and a sponsor does not control the committee calendar alone. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

columns.t: Typical days to the final vote

rows.sponsor: No sponsor named (sent by a department)

sources.t: San Francisco Board of Supervisors: legislation records with dates, sponsors and action history (Legistar; each row links to its file)
